messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

message.content:
Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe. Its key properties include:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, no neutrons), Deuterium (²H, 1 neutron), Tritium (³H, 2 neutrons) |
| **State at STP** | Gas |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, etc. |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺), and metallic bonds (in metal hydrides). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, petroleum refining), laboratory reagent, rocket propellant. |

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, especially its lightness, high reactivity, and importance in both chemistry and astrophysics.
